# Extensibility Request Implementation

The implementation automation supports two repository-configured modes through the
`EXT_REQ_IMPLEMENTATION_MODE` repository variable:

- `per-issue` implements an eligible issue when it receives the `ext-ready-to-implement` label.
  This is also the default when the variable is not defined.
- `per-team` defers implementation to the scheduled team workflow. It combines `event-request`
  and `request-for-external` issues in team PRs, while every other request type gets its own branch
  and draft PR during the same scheduled run.
- `disabled` disables both automatic implementation modes.

The team workflow runs every day at 18:10 Europe/Copenhagen time. For each team and run, it
processes at most five combined requests. It also processes at most five standalone requests total
across all selected teams. Each queue is ordered by oldest `updatedAt` timestamp first:

- `Team: Finance`
- `Team: SCM`
- `Team: Integrations`

An issue must be open, have type `Task`, carry `ext-ready-to-implement`, have exactly one team
label, have exactly one request-type label, and have no open pull request that closes it.
The combined queues contain `event-request` and `request-for-external` issues and produce one team
PR per selected team. The global standalone queue contains the other supported request types and
produces one PR per issue. After the oldest eligible issues are selected up to the applicable
limits, the remaining issues wait for the next scheduled run. A team with no eligible issues
completes successfully without creating a branch or pull request.

Each issue is processed sequentially in an isolated worktree. An implemented issue produces one
commit and reports `changed: true`; any result without a code change reports `changed: false` and
is skipped without modifying the issue. The explanation is informational and does not control the
workflow. The orchestrator uses the actual Git history as the source of truth and normalizes
contradictory `changed` or commit-SHA metadata. Missing results, non-boolean `changed` values,
multiple issue commits, non-AL commits, and dirty worktrees still fail that issue.

Each combined team job writes an issue-outcome list to the workflow run summary. Every selected
issue is shown as implemented, no code change, skipped, or failed, together with the worker's
explanation when available. This makes already-implemented and other no-change results visible
even when the run creates no pull request.

The workflow creates one draft pull request per team and local calendar date. Re-running the same
team on the same date updates its open pull request. If a generated branch exists without an open
pull request, the next run resets that stranded branch to the current default branch and retries
the eligible issues instead of carrying unpublished commits forward. Runs for the same team are
serialized so two scheduled or manual executions cannot publish the same branch concurrently.

The standalone pull request structure is defined directly in the implementation skill. The batch
pull request wrapper is generated by the finalizer. Its `EXT_REQ_BATCH_END` marker is retained so
same-day reruns can append new issue sections without replacing existing ones.

## Telemetry

Telemetry remains issue-based. Team-batch events use the same lifecycle tags as per-issue
implementation and reference the shared pull request. The existing implementation telemetry table
must include this additional column:

```kusto
BatchId:string
```

The sender uses `.set-or-append` with `extend_schema=true`, allowing the configured identity to add
the column automatically when it has Database Admin permission. Otherwise, add the column before
enabling `per-team` mode. Per-issue events store an empty `BatchId`; team events use values such as
`finance-2026-09-08`.
